 More Recalled Breakfast Foods Affected by Listeria Concerns—Here’s What We Know So Far
 DreamBigPhotos/Getty Images 
 By 
 Alex Vance 
 Published on Nov. 20, 2026
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 From grab-and-go sandwiches to frozen meals, see where they were distributed and what consumers should do next.
 We all know the importance of starting the day off strong with a hearty breakfast. When it comes to what we eat, certain options are certainly healthier than others, but sometimes the convenience of a grab-and-go breakfast sandwich wins out.
 Unfortunately, certain biscuits have been under scrutiny in recent weeks. Earlier this month, we reported that Fresh & Ready Foods recalled certain ready-to-eat breakfast sandwiches over concerns about potential Listeria contamination. Now, additional breakfast products are affected—and a biscuit recall appears to be the common thread.
 How the Listeria concerns unfolded
 On November 8, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reported that Fresh & Ready Foods was recalling 2,414 Fresh to You sausage, egg, and cheese biscuit sandwiches because they contained biscuits previously recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son over potential Listeria contamination.
 Soon after, on November 14, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) issued a public health alert for additional ready-to-eat products containing the recalled biscuits. The notice states that the problem was discovered “when a firm notified FSIS that they had received FDA-regulated biscuits that had been recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son.”
 As of November 17, Fresh & Ready Foods expanded its original recall to include additional Fresh to You sandwiches and Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy.
 Now, in the latest development on November 19, Grand Strand Sandwich Company recalled several varieties of breakfast sandwiches over potential Listeria contamination. While the company’s announcement does not explicitly name C.H. Guenther & Son, it states that supplier Dot Foods notified Grand Strand that the biscuits it supplied may be contaminated. C.H. Guenther & Son previously announced in 2021 that its biscuit products were available through Dot Foods.
 Which products are affected?
 The affected products have been identified through the recent company recalls posted by the FDA and a public health alert issued by the USDA’s FSIS. Unlike a recall, a public health alert does not involve a formal product removal.
 Recalled products
 Fresh & Ready Foods 
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich (4.6 oz) 
 SKU: 3100048
 UPC: 8 405493 0168 4 
 Fresh-thru dates: 11/07 – 11/19
 Distribution: Employee break rooms, refrigerated vending machines, and cafeterias between October 25 and November 4, 2026
 States: Oregon and Washington
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich (5.7 oz.) 
 SKU: 3100048
 Fresh-thru dates: 11/12- 11/22
 Distribution: Employee break rooms, Grab & Go coolers, refrigerated vending machines, and micro-markets between October 15, 2026, and November 11, 2026
 States: Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas
 Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy (9.5 oz.) 
 SKU: 90013
 Expiration dates: 11/12 – 11/18
 Distribution: Employee break rooms, Grab & Go coolers, refrigerated vending machines, and micro-markets
 States: Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company 
 The following products were distributed between March 2, 2026, and November 10, 2026, and sold primarily in retail convenience stores, vending machines, and prison canteens in North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia:
 Lunch Box Bacon Egg and Cheese Biscuit (4 oz.) 
 UPC: 0 67068 21400 8 
 Julian date codes (production date codes): 07026; 07526; 08326; 09626; 12526; 13226; 14026; 16826; 17526; 23726
 Lunch Box Chicken Sausage Biscuit (3.75 oz.) 
 UPC: 0 67068 21404 6 
 Julian date code: 06126
 Lunch Box Jumbo Sausage Biscuit (4 oz.) 
 UPC: 0 67068 21407 7 
 Julian date codes: 11126; 11826; 19526
 Lunch Box Sausage Egg & Cheese Biscuit (5 oz.) 
 UPC: 0 67068 21402 2 
 Julian date codes: 11126; 15426; 18226; 20226; 25826; 26426; 29926
 Additional products under the USDA public health alert 
 While most of the affected products are breakfast foods, the USDA’s public health alert also includes other ready-to-eat meals containing the recalled biscuits.
 All affected Granna’s products are listed with best-by dates of 11/01/26 to 10/31/27. They were shipped to a distributor in Oklahoma and subsequently distributed to senior nutrition sites that deliver frozen meals to homes.
 FSIS recommends checking back frequently as it continues to update the list of affected products .
 Granna’s 505 Biscuit and Gravy with Sausage, Hashbrowns, and Flavored Applesauce (15 oz.) 
 EST number: P-46909
 Granna’s 505 Biscuit & Gravy with Meat Crumbles, Flavored Applesauce, and Peaches (15 oz.)  
 EST number: P-27418
 Granna’s 400 Chicken Pot Pie, Green Beans & Pineapples (16 oz.) 
 EST numbers: P-27418; P-46909
 FSIS also includes a photo list of product labels .
 What consumers should do
 Consumers who have any of the affected products should not eat them. The FDA recall announcements advise consumers to discard the recalled sandwiches and other affected foods, while FSIS recommends throwing away or returning products included in its public health alert.
 Anyone who has eaten an affected product should also be aware of the symptoms of a Listeria infection. The FDA  says common symptoms of Listeria infection (listeriosis) include fever, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. In more serious cases, headache, stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance, and convulsions can occur.
 Older adults and people with weakened immune systems are at risk for more serious and sometimes fatal infections. Contact your healthcare provider if you believe you’re experiencing symptoms of Listeria infection.
 To date, no illnesses have been reported in connection with the affected products, according to the recall announcements and FSIS alert.
